title: Bounds during a tape-cleaning return phase
statement: Let $M$ be a $k$-tape Boolean Turing machine, let $q_0$ be a state, and fix an input, a tape index $i$, an input-head position, an initial output, and an integer bound $B$. For an integer $a$, suppose there are a natural number $n$ and tape contents and head positions $D_t,M_t,D_p$ such that $-D_p(i)=n$, $a\le D_p(i)$, tape $M_t(i)$ has its origin mark at $0$ and is blank outside $[a,a-1]$, and every initial head position in $D_p$ has absolute value at most $B$. Starting the cleaned machine in cleaning phase \emph{back} for tape $i$, every configuration through time $n+1$ has every work-tape head position of absolute value at most $B$. At time $n+1$, its state is the next cleaning phase for tape $i$ (or halted if there is no next tape), its first bank of tape contents is unchanged, and both banks' head positions at tape $i$ are reset to $0$ while the second bank's tape $i$ is blank; all other tape contents and positions and the input head and output are unchanged.
